analysis.title: December update: CIO View: Commodities
key_insights: Commodities returned mixed results in 2026, but the CMCI Commodity Total Return Index gained about 25%.
Oil rose sharply after conflict and disruption in the Middle East tightened physical markets. Brent is around USD 92 per barrel, 30% above pre-conflict levels.
Gold hit a record near USD 5,600 an ounce early in 2026, then fell below USD 4,000 as US real yields rose and the dollar firmed.
UBS expects gold headwinds to continue near term. High US real yields and a firm dollar raise the opportunity cost of holding gold and could keep it below USD 4,000 in the short term.
UBS expects structural demand to support gold around USD 4,000 and easing real yields to restore momentum in 2027. It forecasts USD 5,000 an ounce in December 2027 and upgrades gold to Attractive.

UBS expects oil to stay supported in the first half of 2027 by geopolitical tensions and constrained supply. Base case is Brent at USD 90 in June 2027 and USD 80 in December 2027 as supply pressure eases.

Copper is UBS's preferred industrial metal. Electrification, power networks, data centers and AI infrastructure support demand, and long mine-development times constrain supply. UBS recommends adding exposure on weakness.
UBS favors actively managed exposure across energy, industrial metals, agriculture and precious metals, adjusting for inventories, geopolitics, weather, supply discipline and futures curve shape.

sector_views.rationale: Upgraded to Attractive. Structural demand supports prices near USD 4,000 and easing real yields should help a rebound to USD 5,000 by December 2027.
Preferred industrial metal. Demand from electrification, power networks, data centers and AI infrastructure meets supply limited by long mine-development times.
Supported in the first half of 2027 by geopolitical tension and constrained supply, then expected to ease as supply pressure fades. The report gives no explicit rating.
